name: heart-mcp-github
title: The same model, given state instead of a catalogue
html:
The same model, given state instead of a catalogue

Before · pull request #2344, open, mergeable

Offered now: scm:merge scm:close scm:comment scm:edit scm:label scm:request-review scm:update-branch

heart_act · scm:merge · method: squash

acted: “scm:merge was done.” Sent once, with the validator from the state it read. GitHub merged it: 66be32c.

After · closed, merged

Offered now: scm:comment scm:edit scm:label

heart_act · scm:merge, again

rejected-before-sending: “scm:merge is not offered now. Offered: scm:comment, scm:edit, scm:label. Nothing was sent.”

heart_explain · scm:merge

“A closed pull request can’t be merged; reopen it first.”

6tools, never changing: look, act, follow, describe, explain, back
7turns, 22.6 s, Claude Code headless
1act sent to GitHub; the second never left the machine
0addresses, methods or headers shown to the model

Tool search found the six tools. The state came in every answer.

transcript ARTIE’s events
say: Here's the counterpoint, run tonight. Claude Code, headless, with one MCP server: heart-mcp, six tools that never change. Fun detail: Claude Code loaded those six tools with tool search. Tool search found the tools; the state came in every answer. The prompt: open pull request 2344 on the real GitHub test repository, merge it by squashing if it can be merged, then try to merge it again, and report exactly what the service said. Before the merge the service offered seven acts, merge among them. The merge was sent once, with the If-Match validator from the state it read: GitHub merged it, and you can open the pull request and see it. After the merge, three acts were offered. The second merge never left the machine: heart-mcp answered that merge is not offered now, and nothing was sent. Asked why, the service said: a closed pull request can't be merged; reopen it first. Seven turns, twenty-two seconds, and the model never saw an address.
